name: Malaysia
summary_text: Malaysia is dangerous — one of the few countries that criminalises gender expression per se. All 13 states and the Federal Territory prohibit "a man posing as a woman" under Sharia law (up to 3 years in jail, a fine, and caning). While these laws technically apply to Muslims, the enforcement climate affects all trans people: religious police conduct systematic raids on trans events — tipping off media in advance and sharing detainees' faces with tabloids (public outing and humiliation). Three trans women were killed in fewer than two months in 2019. The political climate is shifting toward Islamist parties (a deputy minister urged the "deviant culture" label for LGBTQ; state-backed "rehabilitation" programs; dating-site blocking). For a non-Muslim foreign trans visitor, the Sharia cross-dressing law doesn't directly apply, but being caught in a raided venue, facing the enforcement climate, or being subject to Section 377A (same-sex conduct, 20 years + whipping, applies to all including tourists) are real risks. There is no legal gender recognition.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Malaysia's criminalisation of same-sex activity (Penal Code 377, up to 20 years and whipping) and state Sharia provisions.

sources.title: Malaysia: State-Backed Discrimination Harms LGBT People | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Aug 2022): 'Malaysia: State-Backed Discrimination Harms LGBT People' — documents how state agencies, laws and policies discriminate against LGBT Malaysians.

sources.title: “The Deceased Can’t Speak for Herself:” Violence Against LGBT People in Malaysia | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jun 2019): 'The Deceased Can't Speak for Herself' — violence against LGBT people in Malaysia, following the killing of a transgender woman, with police mistreatment and impunity documented.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (Aug 2023) covers growing LGBTQ fears in Malaysia as Islamists shatter reform hopes.

sources.title: Sauna Raid Highlights Growing Restrictions on Malaysia’s LGBTQ+ Community – The Diplomat
sources.claim_summary: The Diplomat (Dec 2025): a sauna raid highlights growing restrictions on Malaysia's LGBTQ+ community - queer community organisations mobilised to help release over 200 men detained in the raid.

NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (DNS failure); the underlying Human Rights Law Centre case summary covers the Malaysian High Court denying a request to declare Sharia law prohibiting cross-dressing unconstitutional.
NOTE: The UNDP/Asia Pacific Transgender Network publication on Malaysia returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

sources.title: Malaysia: Minister’s order to take action against the transgender community must be revoked | ICJ
sources.claim_summary: ICJ (July 2020): condemned the order by Religious Affairs Minister Zulkifli Mohamad Al-Bakri giving the Federal Territories Islamic Religious Department (Jawi) 'full licence to carry out its enforcement actions' against transgender persons; called for the order to be revoked and for non-discrimination guarantees.

sources.title: LGBTQ in Malaysia: Laws, Rights and Travel
sources.claim_summary: Malaysia4U guide (updated July 2026): the law, Syariah provisions, court rulings and practical guidance for visitors and residents - Sections 377A/377B criminalise 'carnal intercourse against the order of nature' for anyone regardless of gender or consent (up to 20 years plus whipping), including tourists; state Syariah offences (liwat, musahaqah, cross-dressing) apply only to Muslims (max 3 years, RM5,000, 6 strokes); no same-sex marriage or anti-discrimination law; Federal Court struck down Selangor's Section 28 (2021) and 16 Kelantan provisions (2024) on federalism grounds; enforcement against consenting adults in private is uncommon and tourists are rarely targeted.

sources.title: Malaysia: Transgender People Under Threat | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Sept 2014): 'Malaysia: Transgender People Under Threat' - documents arrests of trans women under Sharia laws criminalising 'a male person posing as a woman', violence, and the landmark Court of Appeal ruling finding the Negeri Sembilan law unconstitutional.
